name: ProCC
iocPatterns: Malicious PyPI packages (v1.82.7, v1.82.8) with .pth execution
Cloud infrastructure creations on AWS and Azure
Shell scripts (kamikaze.sh, kube.py) in system paths
Custom strip/cipher protocols for C2 communication
keyCapabilities: Social engineering and impersonation via SMS/Voice
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) bypass and fatigue attacks
Supply chain compromise (PyPI, GitHub Actions, Typosquatting)
Credential dumping from memory and System files (NTDS.dit)
Advanced C2 obfuscation using decentralized protocols (ICP)
Network tunneling via Chisel, Teleport, and rsocx
Automated data exfiltration to cloud storage platforms
Exploitation of high-risk vulnerabilities in common infrastructure software
recommendedActions: Implement strict controls over Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) access.
Rotate stolen NPM tokens and secure CI/CD pipeline keys.
Audit all systems for unauthorized remote management tools like Teleport or rsocx.
Monitor networks for non-standard proxy traffic through Chisel or Ngrok.
Integrate Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) analysis to detect malicious library injections.
campaignsText: ProCC shows a sophisticated evolution from targeted surveillance to broad scale digital infrastructure exploitation. They have moved rapidly into the supply chain, targeting core development components like Trivy and LiteLLM. Their operational tempo is characterized by rapid execution—such as infecting dozens of packages in under 60 seconds—and long-term persistence using decentralized C2 (ICP) and stolen credentials to pivot through cloud environments. Notable campaigns include large-scale data harvesting from cloud providers and the deployment of wiper capabilities for targeted geographic impact.
description: ProCC is a sophisticated threat actor engaged in high-impact supply chain compromises, cloud infrastructure exploitation, and large-scale data theft. The group specializes in bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA) through social engineering and exploiting developer tools to infiltrate vast swaths of industrial and government information.
goals: ProCC's primary objectives include financial gain through data extortion, high-volume credential theft, and potentially intelligence gathering. They target a broad international range of entities in the government, finance, energy, and manufacturing sectors. Their tactics indicate a deliberate move toward targeting developer-centric infrastructure (CI/CD pipelines) to maximize the impact of infection across numerous separate organizations simultaneously.
